Natalism (Be Fruitful and Multiply)
NAY-tuh-liz-uhm
noun (Christian ethics)
From Latin natalis, of birth, from nasci, to be born. The conviction that the bearing of children is a blessing to be welcomed, not a burden to be avoided.

📖 Biblical Definition

Natalism is the biblical conviction that children are a blessing and a heritage from the LORD, and that the bearing of them is good. The first word God spoke to man was a blessing of fruitfulness: "And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth" (Gen 1:28). The Psalmist sings the same, "Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward. As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them" (Psa 127:3-5), and again, "thy children like olive plants round about thy table" (Psa 128:3). Throughout Scripture a full womb is a token of favour and barrenness a grief, for God opens and closes the womb according to His good pleasure. Children are not an accident to be managed away nor a drain upon the earth, but a reward, a quiverful, a heritage. This does not bind every conscience to a precise number, for the LORD gives to one many and to another few; but it forbids the spirit that despises fruitfulness. This dictionary confesses children to be a blessing of the LORD, and rebukes the barren spirit of the age.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Natalism is the conviction that children are a blessing and heritage of the LORD. God's first word to man was be fruitful and multiply. The Psalms call a quiverful of children a reward, not a burden.

expand to see more

NATALISM, noun. The biblical conviction that the bearing of children is a blessing of God to be welcomed.

Grounded in the creation mandate: "Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth" (Gen 1:28).

"Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward" (Psa 127:3).

It requires the welcoming of children as a reward and the rebuke of the spirit that despises them.

It promises the blessing of a full house and a quiver full of arrows.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 1:28 — "And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth."

Psa 127:3 — "Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward."

Psa 127:5 — "Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate."

Psa 128:3 — "Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house: thy children like olive plants round about thy table."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The progressive and anti-natalist spirit of the age treats children as a burden upon the planet and a threat to self, and population-control schemes would suppress the blessing God commanded.

expand to see more

A barren spirit grips the age. The anti-natalist movement reckons the bearing of children a selfish act, even a harm to the planet, and progressive population-control schemes have long pressed to suppress fertility in the name of crisis. Children are recast as a cost, a limit upon ambition, a strain upon resources — never the heritage and reward that the Scripture names them.

Against this the church confesses the first blessing God ever spoke: be fruitful and multiply. Children are an heritage of the LORD and the fruit of the womb His reward; happy is the man whose quiver is full. The church does not bind every conscience to a number, for the LORD apportions the womb as He wills; but it refuses the lie that fruitfulness is a curse, and it welcomes children as the gift God declared them to be.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The roots are the creation mandate to be fruitful and the Psalms' praise of children as a heritage of the LORD.

expand to see more

Natalis (Latin), of birth — the welcoming of new life as good.

Genesis 1:28 gives the first blessing: be fruitful and multiply.

Psalm 127 names children a heritage and the fruit of the womb a reward.

Psalm 128 pictures the children like olive plants round the table.

Throughout Scripture the LORD opens and closes the womb according to His pleasure.

Usage

"Their natalism welcomed each child as a heritage of the LORD rather than a burden."

"A biblical natalism rebukes the anti-natalist spirit that calls children a cost to the planet."

"He read Psalm 127 and saw his quiverful as the reward Scripture promised."
